summary: Round 2: five reviewer findings fixed on the same branch. (1) A review whose every remaining finding was a refuted absence claim is no longer upgraded to APPROVED — it becomes NEEDS_HUMAN with a 'review verdict' finding and routes to blocked, so a refuted claim neither requeues a round nor accepts a task. (2) Absence checks now split existence claims (checked against the worktree) from visibility claims ('not supplied / truncated', checked against the supplied patch and the archived truncation manifest; undecidable -> unchecked, never refuted). (3) The sensitive-file strip records the paths it withholds, so they appear in the manifest and in the reviewer-visible omission marker instead of vanishing. (4) A partially supplied file carries an inline '[review diff: N of M hunks shown ...]' marker naming the omitted hunk headers, and is listed as 'partially included' rather than 'included'. (5) The diff is ordered source-first and prefers whole files, so with this branch's own diff all source files except review_service.py are complete and that one is 7 of 9 hunks with the two omitted hunk headers named inline; max_diff_tokens is unchanged. Round-1 work (archived review_payload.md with truncation manifest, PROPOSED CCR-T11-01, harness vs model absence sections, diff-completeness / .gitattributes findings) is intact.

assumptions: The evidence files are stamped at 96289d7 with tree=0 dirty-entries; the commit that carries this index (4eb490d) changes only verify-evidence/T-11/**, never source or tests, so 554 passed / 6 skipped / lint clean are the counts for the code under review.
T-11 DoD 1 explicitly grants the review_payload.md archive and orders a PROPOSED CCR; the name stays PROPOSED and docs/frozen-contracts.md is not edited.

review.json keeps its frozen shape: absence provenance lives in the existing notes and missing_artifacts arrays with harness-detected:/reviewer-asserted: labels, plus prose notes; no new key and no new verdict value.

A refuted claim routes to the existing NEEDS_HUMAN (-> blocked). That is a routing decision inside the allowed verdict vocabulary, not a change to who may accept a task: nothing is accepted on a refuted claim any more, and no finding is silently dropped without being recorded.

Whether a claim is an existence claim or a visibility claim is decided from its wording ('missing' vs 'not supplied/truncated/not visible'); a composite claim such as 'missing from the supplied artifacts and the worktree' is treated as a visibility claim, which can only be unchecked, never refuted — fail closed.
Per-file expectations come from git diff --numstat --no-renames base...HEAD (not from parsing the archived --stat text, which abbreviates long paths): the same comparison, unabbreviated.
An attribute already set at the merge-base is reported as pre-existing and informational (blocks=False), so an older repository setting cannot fail an unrelated run.
Diff budget is not widened: max_diff_tokens is unchanged; files are ordered source-first and whole files are preferred so the wiring is supplied complete where the budget allows.
questions: Operator decision requested: approve CCR-T11-01 to add runs/<run_id>/review_payload.md to the frozen artifact layout, or leave it unfrozen as on this branch.

With max_diff_tokens=12000 and ~22k tokens of changes on this branch, review_service.py is still supplied as 7 of 9 hunks (the two omitted hunk headers are named inline and the file is fully present in the repo). If the operator wants whole-file review for diffs this size, max_diff_tokens has to be raised — that is a harness setting change, not something this DoD authorises.

memory_suggestions.content: A deterministic gate that 'refutes' a claim must know which sense of absence is being claimed: existence on disk is not visibility to the reviewer. Treat existence checks as refutation only for repository claims; a claim about supplied artifacts has to be checked against the supplied bytes (patch + archive manifest) and be marked unchecked when that is impossible. And never let a refuted claim upgrade a verdict — route to a human instead, because refuting an accusation is not verification.

coding-orchestrator review prompts have two independent budgets: max_diff_tokens (~12k) for the diff section and max_prompt_context_tokens (~60k) for the whole prompt; enforce_budget can additionally middle-cut the already-budgeted dynamic_state section, which is why review_audit.supplied_evidence marks per-file visibility 'unchecked' whenever a context_budget truncation hit dynamic_state. Measured on T-11: a branch diff of ~22k tokens cannot be fully supplied at 12k, so prompt_builder orders files source-first and prefers whole files (one silent middle cut mid-file is what made a reviewer call the wiring unverifiable).
